exercise.name: Reverse-Grip Bench Press
library_steps: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar palms facing you, shoulder-width.
Lower the bar slowly to your lower chest, elbows tucked in.
Press it back up; use a spotter, as this grip can slip.
exercise.one_line_summary: Flat bench, straight bar held palms toward the face (supinated), hands about shoulder width (~45-50 cm, 1.0-1.2x); start arms straight with the bar over the lower chest; lower to touch the lower chest (sternum / bottom of the breastbone) with elbows tucked ~30-35 deg from the body; press back up. Triceps and chest (upper chest favoured by the grip) share the work; front delt helps.

setup.why: Library step; S1 and S2 tested the flat bench.

setup.target: Head, upper back and hips on the pad, feet flat on the floor.
Palms toward the face (supinated), thumbs wrapped round the bar, wrists stacked over the forearms.
setup.why: Defines the exercise; S2 used a closed thumb grip for both grips. The library warns the grip can slip.

setup.target: About shoulder width: ~45-50 cm between hand centres (1.0-1.2x shoulder / biacromial width).
setup.why: Library: shoulder-width. S1 and S2 tested 100 % biacromial (close) supinated; S3 says a little wider than the shoulders is fine.

movement.end: 95 deg (bar on the lower chest, forearms near vertical)

movement.measure: upper arm from the torso side line, 0 = by the side (the elbow tuck)
movement.start: 80 deg (arms vertical, bar over the lower chest)

movement.measure: 0 = out to the side, +90 = straight up from the chest, negative = below the torso line
movement.end: -25 deg (elbows a little below the bench line)

movement.start: over the lower chest, arms vertical
movement.end: touching the lower chest at the bottom of the breastbone (between nipple line and xiphoid)
movement.tolerance: touch point within 5 cm of the xiphoid toward the head; no bounce

movement.start: flat on the bench, feet on floor

muscles.emg: Bench press: triceps and pectoralis similar and both above the front delt (S4). Supinated grip gave somewhat LESS long-head triceps than a close pronated grip (S2); grip narrowing raised lateral-head triceps regardless of supination (S1).
muscles.role: Straightens the elbows; library primary (joint-top with chest).

muscles.anatomy: Pectoralis major, clavicular and sternocostal parts
muscles.emg: Supinated grip raised clavicular pectoralis over pronated on a flat bench (S1, isometric). In full reps the supinated flat grip did not beat wide pronated for the clavicular head and lowered the sternocostal head (S2).
muscles.role: Brings the arms forward and up; library primary. Upper chest gain is study-dependent, so the whole chest mask is lit.
muscles.surface: Front of the chest from collarbone to lower breastbone.

muscles.emg: Significantly below triceps and chest in the bench press, but a named mover (S4); listed as worked in the reverse-grip press (S3).
muscles.role: Helps raise the upper arm; library secondary, two sources.

muscles.emg: Higher with the supinated grip than pronated (S1).
muscles.role: Steadies the elbow; not a mover, not in the library, so not lit.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arms near 70-90 deg out from the body at the bottom.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library cue is elbows tucked; S2 measured ~34 deg at the close grip versus ~68 deg at the wide grip.

mistakes.mistake: Bar to the upper chest or neck
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Bar comes down near the collarbones.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library and S3 put the bar on the lower chest / bottom of the breastbone.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Thumbs on the same side of the bar as the fingers.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The library warns this grip can slip; S2 used a closed thumb grip.

sources.citation: Lehman GJ. 2005. The influence of grip width and forearm pronation/supination on upper-body myoelectric activity during the flat bench press. J Strength Cond Res 19(3):587-591.
sources.what_it_gave: 12 men, isometric holds, 5 grips: supinated grip raised biceps and clavicular pectoralis; narrower grip raised triceps.

sources.citation: Arseneault K, Roy X, Sercia P. 2021. The effect of 12 variations of the bench press exercise on the EMG activity of three heads of the pectoralis major. Int J Strength Cond 1(1). doi 10.47206/ijsc.v1i1.39.
sources.what_it_gave: 13 trained men, full reps at 12RM, 100 % / 200 % biacromial grips, pronated and supinated, closed thumb grip; shoulder abduction 33.6 +- 2.1 deg (close) vs 67.9 +- 3.3 deg (wide); close pronated beat supinated for triceps long head; supinated 1RM ~17 % lower.

sources.citation: Read T (CPT); medically reviewed by Bubnis D (MS, NASM-CPT). 2021. Reverse grip bench press. Healthline.
sources.what_it_gave: Palms facing you, a little wider than the shoulders; lower until the bar is at about the sternum and xiphoid; no bouncing; muscles: upper chest, biceps, triceps, front delt.

sources.citation: Stastny P, Golas A, Blazek D, et al. 2017. A systematic review of surface electromyography analyses of the bench press movement task. PLoS One 12(2):e0171632.
sources.what_it_gave: 14 studies: triceps and pectoralis major similar and both significantly above the front delt in the bench press.

clip_check.check: Hands 40-60 cm apart, palms toward the face, thumbs round the bar
Start: arms straight and vertical, bar over the lower chest
End: bar touching the lower chest (not inside it), elbows tucked
clip_check.target: elbow 95, elev 35, plane -25; bar clear 0-0.01 m

clip_check.check: Back on pad, feet on floor
Triceps and chest strongest red in both pictures; front delt light red
